content.text:
All six findings are fixed, each with tests. `make test`, `make lint` and the frontend typecheck and unit tests pass; I did not run `make e2e` or click through the two frontend fixes in a browser. Nothing is committed.

| # | Fix | Test |
|---|---|---|
| F1 | Approve sends the revision shown in the editor. A clean draft refreshes when a newer revision loads. An edited draft is kept, marked as a conflict, and blocks Approve until resolved. | `useDraft.test.ts`: conflict, reload, second approval, checking displayed copy and submitted revision id. |
| F2 | The limiter token is now taken after the claim and render, as the last step before the provider call. | `TestStalledClaimsDoNotBurstTheProvider` stalls 20 claims, releases them together and counts dispatch times. With the old order restored it fails with 117 calls in one second. |
| F3 | The fixed TLD list is replaced: any dotted host whose last label is 2+ letters or punycode is rejected, including IDNs. | New fixtures for `evil.click`, `evil.top`, `evil.zip?next=login`, Turkish, Cyrillic, Japanese and punycode hosts, plus benign dotted text that must pass. |
| F4 | The worker runs `delivery.Reconcile` every 30 s to close what a discarded River job left open. | `reconcile_db_test.go` covers send (including a message left in `sending`), generation and fan-out, each run twice to show it is idempotent. |
| F5 | The claim checks the 6-attempt and 15-minute budget atomically. An exhausted message goes `dead` with no provider call. | `TestExhaustedMessagesAreNotSentAgain`, and `TestDeadAfterMaxAge` now asserts zero calls. |
| F6 | Loading a `generation_failed` campaign replays its event stream, so the errors show after a refresh. No backend change was needed. | `useGeneration.test.ts` replays a finished failed stream. The mount-time trigger in `CampaignView.vue` has no test, since there is no component test setup. |

Decisions I made that you should confirm (candidates for `DECISIONS.md`):

- **F2 trade-off:** a cancel or consent change that lands during the token wait (about 0.2 s at most) is no longer seen, the same as one landing during the HTTP call. The two `...WhileWaitingForToken` tests became `...BeforeClaim` and now revoke just before the claim query.
- **F3 false positive:** a sentence with no space after its period, such as `Kaçırma.Hemen gel`, is now rejected as a domain. The error message tells the writer to add the space.
- **F4 fan-out:** an `approved` campaign whose fan-out job is discarded or cancelled moves to `cancelled` (actor `worker`, reason `fan-out failed`). The alternative is to re-enqueue the fan-out; I chose cancel to avoid a retry loop.
- **F4 and F5 unknown outcomes:** a message stuck in `sending` when its budget or job runs out becomes `dead` with a last error saying the outcome is unknown. It is not reconciled against the provider, so it may have been delivered once.
- **F4 timing:** River's default is 25 attempts, so a job takes weeks to be discarded. The reconciler only acts then. Lowering `MaxAttempts` per job kind would shorten this; I left it alone.

I also updated `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (send job steps, rate limit test, a new "Exhausted jobs" paragraph, failed-generation replay).

Suggested commit message:

```
Fix six review findings in approval, delivery and link policy.

Bind approval to the revision on screen. Take the rate-limit token
right before the provider call. Reject any literal domain, not only
listed TLDs. Reconcile messages and campaigns left by discarded River
jobs. Enforce the retry budget at claim time. Replay generation errors
when a failed campaign is loaded.
```

content.thinking: The rate limiter spaces tokens 10 ms apart but the test times the provider calls, so a delayed goroutine lets a 1 s window fit 102 calls against a limit of 100. Moving the token next to the call narrows the gap, but no ordering removes it, so I'll look at other fixes next.

options.label: Headroom (Recommended)
options.description: Space tokens so 100 calls take 1.05 s (about 95/s). Absorbs up to 50 ms of dispatch delay, the test asserts <=100 strictly. Rule 8 is a cap, so 95/s still complies. Changes TestLimiterSettings and the ARCHITECTURE rate paragraph.

options.label: Loosen the test
options.description: Keep 100/s and allow a few extra calls in the dispatch test. Simplest, but it accepts small real excesses over 100/s under load.

options.label: Sliding-window gate

docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:185:4. Render the payload, then wait for a rate-limit token. The token is the last step before the call. No database work sits between the token and the request, so a slow claim or a busy pool cannot bunch calls together. The cost: a cancel or a consent change that lands during the wait (at most 20 workers / 100 per second, about 0.2 s) is not seen, the same as one that lands during the HTTP call.
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:212:**Rate limit** (rule 8): one `rate.Limiter` per channel in the worker, 100 tokens/s. Every provider call takes a token, retries included, because every attempt hits the provider. Burst is 1 (at most 10). With a burst of 100, a full bucket plus a second of refill could let close to 200 through in one second; with burst 1, any 1-second window holds at most 100 sends. The worker is the only process that sends. Running more worker replicas needs a shared limiter (documented limitation). A second test stalls every claim, releases them together, and counts real dispatch times: no 1 s window exceeds 100. The limiter test runs inside a `testing/synctest` bubble, whose fake clock only advances when every goroutine is blocked. 500 goroutines hammer the limiter for 10 virtual seconds, and the test asserts no 1 s window exceeds 100 and total throughput is close to 1,000. If `x/time/rate` does not cooperate with the bubble, the limiter moves behind a small `Clock` interface (to be checked first thing when this is built).
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:227:- `queued` and never attempted 2 minutes after fan-out (`not_started`; nothing drains the queue, for example the worker is down). At 100/s that is 12,000 messages per channel, more than the whole seed.

content.text:
I fixed the failing test by giving the limiter headroom. It now hands out one token every 10.5 ms, so 100 tokens take 1.05 s, about 95 per second. `make test` and `make lint` pass, but I couldn't re-run the failing test under `-race` here, so the exact CI path isn't confirmed yet.

**Why it failed.** The failure was a real overshoot, not just a flaky assertion. The limiter spaced tokens exactly 10 ms apart, but the test times the actual provider calls. Between taking a token and making the call, the program can be paused for a moment, and in CI under `-race` that was about 20 ms. If an early call is delayed and the next ones aren't, one second can hold 102 calls. At exactly 100 per second there is no room for any delay. With the headroom, any delay under 50 ms still keeps every one-second window at 100 calls or fewer.

**Changes:**
- `internal/delivery/limiter.go`: added `Headroom = 50ms` and `Interval = (1s + Headroom) / 100`.
- `limiter_test.go`: checks the 10.5 ms spacing. On the fake clock it asserts that no 1.05 s window holds more than 100 tokens and that 10 s gives about 950 tokens.
- `send_db_test.go`: the dispatch test now asserts at most 100 calls per second strictly, so the "+1" allowance is gone.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`: the rule 8 row and the rate limit paragraph now explain the headroom, the reason for it, and that it costs about 5% of throughput.

**Not verified.** The secrets hook blocked my stress run (the dispatch test 15 times under `-race` with background CPU load), most likely because the command contained `env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. Per CLAUDE.md I didn't try to get around it. To check it yourself, start the test database first (`make test` does this), then run:

```bash
env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY TEST_DATABASE_URL='postgres://postgres:test@127.0.0.1:55432/postgres?sslmode=disable' REQUIRE_DB=1 go test -race -count=15 -run TestStalledClaimsDoNotBurstTheProvider ./internal/delivery/
```

**Your file.** `DECISIONS.md` item 13 still says "100/sn, burst 1". You may want to add the 50 ms headroom there.

Suggested commit message:

```
Leave 50 ms of headroom in the per-channel rate limiter.

A call can lag its token. At exactly 100/s a 20 ms lag let 102 calls
into one second under -race in CI. One token every 10.5 ms keeps any
1 s window at 100 or fewer as long as the lag stays under 50 ms.
```
